title: LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form
knob_name: whitened least-squares projection (all-or-nothing; optional partial interpolation)
forget_metric: linear guardedness (no linear probe can recover concept)
utility_metric: perplexity / downstream probe accuracy (no headline utility table extracted)
low_dose_frontier_quality: excellent in principle: provably minimal change under any norm in the class
near_collapse_behaviour: no collapse regime — closed-form projection cannot diverge
notes: Verified via arXiv abs page. Guarantee is LINEAR erasure only: nothing stops nonlinear recovery, and 'the sea' is unlikely to be a single linear direction. Abstract page gives no utility-loss numbers; I did not confirm any collateral table. Composes trivially over 30 days (projections stack) but each projection eats a rank-1 subspace per layer — cumulative rank loss is the risk.

title: Null It Out: Guarding Protected Attributes by Iterative Nullspace Projection
max_sequential_interventions: many (iterations are inherently sequential; ~10-300 reported in literature)
low_dose_frontier_quality: good but iterations are the dose: each removes a direction
near_collapse_behaviour: progressive representation damage as iterations accumulate (LEACE paper's stated motivation)
notes: Verified (ACL 2020). Direct precedent for REPEATED linear erasure, which is the T1 sequential question. Abstract page carries no numbers on representation damage from repeated projection; superseded by LEACE for single-concept minimality.

title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
base_model: 13 chat models incl. Gemma 7B, Qwen 1.8-72B, Llama-2/3
low_dose_frontier_quality: best measured ratio in T1: near-total behavioural erasure for ≤1.4pt utility loss
near_collapse_behaviour: no collapse — rank-1 weight edit is bounded
notes: Table 3 deltas: Gemma 7B MMLU +0.1 ARC +0.2 GSM8K -0.7 TruthfulQA -2.4; Yi 34B MMLU -1.4 TruthfulQA -3.5; Qwen 72B MMLU -0.7. <$5 compute for a 70B model. Caveat: refusal is a BEHAVIOUR with one clean direction; a semantic concept like 'bread' may not be rank-1. No sequential-composition experiment.

title: Erasing Conceptual Knowledge from Language Models (ELM)
knob_name: LoRA rank / eta guidance strength / layer span
low_dose_frontier_quality: strongest LLM forget:collateral ratio among trained methods
near_collapse_behaviour: not swept; fluency preserved where RMU degrades it (R-PPL 10.9 vs RMU 24.8)
notes: LoRA rank 4, eta=500, layers 4-7 — directly QLoRA-shaped and the closest published analogue to the day-N erasure step. Self-classifier objective. No sequential/repeated-erasure experiment reported; no compute cost stated.

title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use With Unlearning (RMU)
knob_name: steering coefficient c / layer l / steps
low_dose_frontier_quality: headline numbers look benign, but no dose-response sweep is published
near_collapse_behaviour: not characterised in the paper — matches in-project finding that the low-dose end is undocumented
notes: Updates only layers l-2, l-1, l with loss on layer l. Paper does NOT report the layer number, coefficient, step count, batch size or runtime in text — those live only in code. That absence is exactly why the in-project step-29→30 cliff was a surprise: no published sweep exists.

title: On Effects of Steering Latent Representation for Large Language Model Unlearning
knob_name: steering coefficient c (swept 1/2/5/10) and layer index
low_dose_frontier_quality: the only published c-sweep — forgetting rises with c but MMLU falls sharply
near_collapse_behaviour: explicit sharp tradeoff: larger c improves forgetting but causes 'significant drop' on MMLU
notes: Mechanistic account of WHY the transition is sharp: convergence requires the l2-norm of forget-sample representations to fall below c, so the loss only converges in early layers — a threshold condition, not a smooth dial. RMU works layers 3-10 and fails 11-31. Directly explains the in-project cliff.

title: Negative Preference Optimization: From Catastrophic Collapse to Effective Unlearning
forget_metric: first method to reach workable unlearning at 50% forget fraction
low_dose_frontier_quality: better than GA but still a divergent objective
near_collapse_behaviour: theory: divergence to collapse is exponentially SLOWER than gradient ascent, but still divergent
notes: The key structural insight for the decay/forget split: GA-family losses are unbounded, so 'dose' is training time and collapse is asymptotic rather than a plateau. GA already fails at 10% forget. Numbers here are TOFU-style, not concept-erasure.

title: Simplicity Prevails: Rethinking Negative Preference Optimization for LLM Unlearning
low_dose_frontier_quality: claims better forget-utility frontier than NPO via removing reference-model bias
near_collapse_behaviour: not characterised
notes: Verified title/venue. I could NOT confirm specific forget/utility numbers from the abstract page — do not cite numbers for this row. Relevant mechanism: reference-model bias causes uneven per-sample optimization, i.e. the effective dose differs per example — a plausible contributor to cliff behaviour.

title: On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning
forget_metric: per-request forget efficacy on ScienceQA / TOFU / CLINC150
utility_metric: World Facts, Real Authors, MRPC/RTE utility
low_dose_frontier_quality: the only clean demonstration that ORTHOGONAL adapters stop cumulative collateral
near_collapse_behaviour: baselines collapse fast: GradAsc hits 0% utility by request 2; SOGD ~2-4%
notes: Numbers: O3 holds ~88-89% utility across all 3 requests (TOFU) and 87-89% (CLINC150); EUL drops 88.1→76.3 on RTE by request 3; GradAsc 0% by request 2. Only 3-4 requests, not 30 — the sequential-composition evidence is thin at our horizon. Orthogonal-LoRA-per-day is the directly transferable recipe.

title: FIT to Forget: Robust Continual Unlearning for Large Language Models
method_family: filtering + importance-aware method selection + layer attribution
utility_metric: claims preserved GSM8K/MMLU after hundreds of requests
low_dose_frontier_quality: claimed strong but unverified
near_collapse_behaviour: identifies the mechanism: overlapping gradients across requests accumulate and suppress common tokens → collapse
notes: Verified title/authors/date on arXiv abs. I could NOT extract the results tables — no numbers cited here. The mechanism claim (shared-lexical-dimension gradient accumulation causing systematic common-token suppression) is the single best published explanation of what a 30-day sequential forget arm will do to a model.

title: Unlearning Isn't Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
knob_name: learning rate x number of requests
utility_metric: retain accuracy and PCA representational drift
low_dose_frontier_quality: directly maps the low-dose end: at LR 5e-6, 100 requests, retain acc 6.2% RECOVERS to 65% after relearning
near_collapse_behaviour: at LR 3e-5 the same 100 requests are irreversible: forget 0.05% stays 2.1% after relearning; PCA drift 133.2 vs ~1-11 reversible
notes: The strongest direct evidence for H1's repair clause: whether collateral is repairable is controlled by LEARNING RATE, and the reversible/irreversible boundary is visible in representation-space drift (PCA distance ~1-11 vs >100) even when task metrics look identical. Gives a per-day go/no-go instrument.

title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
max_sequential_interventions: not tested sequentially (simultaneous multi-task addition only)
low_dose_frontier_quality: genuinely graded: lambda is a real continuous dial with a published sweep
near_collapse_behaviour: no cliff reported — degradation is smooth in lambda
notes: The ONLY family in T1 with a published smooth dose-response over a fine lambda grid, and the cheapest to compute (one fine-tune per concept, then arithmetic). Toxicity: 6x reduction for +0.5 PPL. Vision numbers dominate the paper; the LM evidence is a single toxicity experiment. Sequential composition untested at n=30.

title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
knob_name: number of merged vectors; trim ratio (top-k %)
low_dose_frontier_quality: quantifies interference growth directly
near_collapse_behaviour: performance degrades monotonically with count: ~100% at 2 tasks, ~85% at 7, ~80% at 11; task arithmetic falls faster
notes: Composition, not erasure — but this is the closest published curve for 'what happens when you stack N weight-space edits'. Extrapolating 2→7→11 to 30 predicts substantial cumulative loss without a repair stage. Sign-conflict and redundancy are the named causes; both apply to 30 stacked forget vectors.

title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch (DARE)
low_dose_frontier_quality: shows an erasure update can be 99% sparsified with no measured loss — a free collateral reduction
near_collapse_behaviour: not applicable
notes: Not an erasure method, but a directly usable collateral-shrinking wrapper: if a day-N forget vector survives 90-99% dropout, the update touches ~1% of deltas and 30 days of edits overlap far less. Numbers are for capability-preserving merges, NOT for erasure vectors — untested in our direction.

title: SAEs Can Improve Unlearning: Dynamic Sparse Autoencoder Guardrails for Precision Unlearning in LLMs
method_family: SAE feature clamping with input-gated guardrail
low_dose_frontier_quality: best published forget:collateral ratio at ~2B scale
near_collapse_behaviour: forward-pass only, no gradient divergence, so no collapse regime
notes: Closest model match in the whole thread (Gemma-2-2b-it, Gemma Scope SAE). Reports maintaining the ideal region across sequential requests where others degrade. CAVEAT for our design: DSG is an INFERENCE-TIME gated intervention, not a weight-space update, so it is not QLoRA-shaped without adaptation — and a gate that only fires on detected inputs is arguably not erasure.

title: Applying sparse autoencoders to unlearn knowledge in language models
knob_name: number of features (10/20/50), clamp value (~-18 to -20)
utility_metric: MMLU and unrelated MCQ side effects
low_dose_frontier_quality: honest negative result: worse collateral than RMU at matched forgetting
near_collapse_behaviour: zero-ablation does nothing; effect only appears past a large negative clamp — another threshold nonlinearity
notes: Two findings that matter: (1) zero-ablating features is INEFFECTIVE — you must clamp to ~-18/-20, i.e. the response is threshold-like not proportional, mirroring the in-project cliff; (2) 10 features beat 20 and 50, so narrower readout = less collateral. Gemma-2-2b, same family as our target.

title: Erasing Concepts from Diffusion Models (ESD)
knob_name: negative guidance strength; ESD-x (cross-attn only) vs ESD-u (unconditional/full)
forget_metric: artist style / NSFW / object class removal
utility_metric: human eval and interference on other artists
low_dose_frontier_quality: localisation IS the knob: ESD-x limits the edit to cross-attention and preserves neighbours; ESD-u is broader and damages more
near_collapse_behaviour: known to over-erase neighbouring concepts
notes: The canonical demonstration that WHERE you edit determines collateral, independent of how hard you edit — the transferable lesson for choosing a layer span on gemma-3-4b. Abstract page gives no interference numbers; the comparative numbers I did extract come from RECE and MACE tables instead.

title: Unified Concept Editing in Diffusion Models (UCE)
knob_name: number of concepts edited (1..100); preserved-concept set
low_dose_frontier_quality: closed-form, training-free, ~1.2s per concept — extremely cheap dose
near_collapse_behaviour: degrades with edit count: specificity falls to 61.78% at 100 concepts
notes: Numbers above are as reported in the MACE comparison table. This is the best available quantification of MULTI-CONCEPT erasure decay: interference at ~100 concepts costs ~38 points of specificity. Includes an explicit 'preserve' term — the closest analogue to a retain-only healing stage folded into the closed form.

title: MACE: Mass Concept Erasure in Diffusion Models
method_family: closed-form cross-attn refinement + per-concept LoRA + closed-form LoRA fusion
low_dose_frontier_quality: best mass-erasure frontier published: 4.31% efficacy at 84.56% specificity
near_collapse_behaviour: specificity holds far better than UCE (84.56 vs 61.78) at n=100
notes: THE architectural template for a 30-day forget arm: one LoRA per concept, trained separately, then fused in closed form specifically to avoid mutual interference. This is exactly the composition problem T1 asks about, solved at n=100 in the diffusion setting. Untested for LLMs.

title: Reliable and Efficient Concept Erasure of Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (RECE)
forget_metric: nudity: 66 detected parts vs UCE 186, ESD-u 121; erased object classes 0.3% acc vs ESD-u 12.6%
low_dose_frontier_quality: strong: near-total erasure for ~0.3 CLIP points
near_collapse_behaviour: not characterised
notes: 3.4s per concept, modifies only 2.23% of UNet params. Demonstrates the resurfacing problem concretely: it derives the embeddings that REGENERATE a supposedly erased concept and erases those too, iteratively. Direct analogue of the day-N re-check of previously erased concepts in our design.

title: Editing as Unlearning: Are Knowledge Editing Methods Strong Baselines for LLM Unlearning?
method_family: rank-one / mass editing (ROME, MEMIT, AlphaEdit, WISE)
knob_name: number of sequential edits; batch size
low_dose_frontier_quality: poor: ROME forgets but takes the retain set with it
near_collapse_behaviour: MEMIT leaves the LLM non-functional (near-zero Rouge1 on BOTH sets); ROME/MEMIT collapse under long edit sequences
notes: Important negative result for the rank-one-editing branch: naive ROME/MEMIT-as-unlearning is NOT a minimal-collateral recipe at our sequence length, and explicitly 'cannot well perform under long sequences of editing'. Their query-merging fix recovers it (ROME 1.622, MEMIT 1.632 combined score vs DPO 1.123). AlphaEdit and WISE were the strongest editors.

title: Unlearning That Lasts: Utility-Preserving, Robust, and Almost Irreversible Forgetting in LLMs
utility_metric: MMLU 59.9 vs 59.6 baseline; Win Rate 0.47 vs 0.5
low_dose_frontier_quality: excellent, and the closest model scale to gemma-3-4b in the thread
near_collapse_behaviour: GradDiff/NPO collapse past ~600 steps; JensUn holds Win Rate 0.46 at 2000 steps
notes: The direct fix for the in-project cliff: the cliff is a property of UNBOUNDED losses (GA/GradDiff/NPO all diverge), and swapping to a BOUNDED objective (JSD) makes the step count a genuine monotone dial over 600-2000 steps instead of a threshold. Relearning: 8% forget acc recovered after 600 relearn steps vs NPO 26%. 3B-scale, single GPU.

title: Erasing Without Collateral Damage: Precise Concept Removal in Diffusion Models (CARE)
utility_metric: retained neighbours IMPROVE: Mickey FID 5.72→4.43, Picasso 6.82→5.86, Marilyn 6.68→3.29
low_dose_frontier_quality: collateral is reduced below the naive-erasure baseline by construction
near_collapse_behaviour: not characterised
notes: Mechanism worth stealing: down-weight the component of the erasure direction that is SHARED with a bank of protected concept anchors, in closed form. That is a cheap, retain-set-aware way to shrink day-N collateral before it happens — complementary to a post-hoc healing fine-tune. Diffusion only; 2026 preprint, unrefereed.

title: Model Editing at Scale leads to Gradual and Catastrophic Forgetting
forget_metric: edit efficacy / recall of prior edits
low_dose_frontier_quality: good below knee: efficacy ~100% until inflection
near_collapse_behaviour: two-phase: gradual decline then abrupt cliff; ROME knee at 100-800 edits (as low as 10); MEMIT gradual to ~4000 edits; paraphrase detection dies long before the cliff
notes: ~30% of previously edited facts forgotten by 600 ROME edits (sample 1); MEMIT ~10% at same count. Canonical two-phase (gradual->catastrophic) curve; feeds the knee-location prior for H4.

title: Model Editing Harms General Abilities of Large Language Models: Regularization to the Rescue
low_dose_frontier_quality: poor for KN: single edit can zero out tasks; ROME/MEMIT tolerable at small N
near_collapse_behaviour: perturbation compounds: ROME weight elements with delta>0.077 grow 20%(1 edit)->49.2%(5)->72.8%(15); KN collapses after 1 edit on LLaMA-1
notes: RECT regularization retains >94% edit success while protecting downstream — evidence that a repair/regularity term buys real budget. Weight-drift metric is a usable leakage proxy.

title: MUSE: Machine Unlearning Six-Way Evaluation for Language Models
low_dose_frontier_quality: acceptable for 1 request for some methods; most degrade by request 2-4
near_collapse_behaviour: GA and NPO collapse to ~zero utility after first requests; utility decreases monotonically with request count for nearly all 8 methods
notes: Sustainability axis = the protocol to copy for H4: 4 sequential folds of 0.8M tokens News corpus; measures utility trend vs request index. Also finds unlearned knowledge resurfaces under paraphrase probing.

title: On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning (O3: Orthogonal LoRA + OOD detector)
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: O3 at request 3 keeps 78.5/80.9 vs base 88.0/88.7 (ScienceQA) with no retain data
near_collapse_behaviour: GradDif and SOGD emit empty/nonsensical repeated tokens by request 2-3; EUL degrades by request 3
notes: Structural isolation (orthogonal LoRA per request) prevents inter-request interference — supports ordering/isolation levers for keeping each day under budget. Uses no retain data at all.

title: Avoiding Copyright Infringement via Large Language Model Unlearning (Stable Sequential Unlearning)
method_family: task-vector negation + random-labeling loss + weight saliency
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: SSU MMLU 0.6625(step1)->0.6425(step5) i.e. ~0.5%/step absolute, stable to step 10
near_collapse_behaviour: GA collapses by step 5 (MMLU 0.58->0.31 Llama; step 1 on Mistral); Task Vector hits MMLU=0 by step 10 (Llama) / step 5 (Mistral); GradDiff MT-Bench 8.03->4.94 at step 5
notes: Closest analogue to our design: ~1 concept(book)/step for 10 steps on an 8B chat model. SSU's ~0.3-0.5% MMLU loss/step is a direct per-cycle leakage estimate; naive methods knee at 5-10 steps.

title: FIT to Forget: Robust Continual Unlearning for Large Language Models
method_family: redundancy filtering + adaptive algorithm selection + targeted layers
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: at 300 requests MMLU 65.56 vs retain-model 65.97, GSM8K 57.02 vs 58.83
near_collapse_behaviour: retain utility sags 0.88(60 req)->0.71(120) then plateaus ~0.70-0.72 to 300; GA/RLabel collapse to near zero
notes: Largest sequential-request count found (300). Shows a sag-then-plateau rather than a cliff when interventions are localized/filtered — favourable shape for H4 at our N=30.

title: Adaptive Localization of Knowledge Negation for Continual LLM Unlearning
low_dose_frontier_quality: >95% utility retained after sufficient sequential unlearning
near_collapse_behaviour: some baselines completely lose utility over the same task sequence
notes: ICML 2025. Key idea for us: adapt unlearning intensity to inter-task (concept) relationships — entangled concepts get gentler doses; supports concept-ordering lever. PDF numbers not fully extracted (compressed PDF).

title: AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing for Language Models
low_dose_frontier_quality: excellent to 3000 edits: original general capability maintained across all metrics
near_collapse_behaviour: MEMIT GLUE F1 approaches zero by 2000 edits; MEMIT efficacy 65.65% vs AlphaEdit 98.90% (LLaMA-3 at 2000)
notes: Projection onto null space of preserved-knowledge keys = mathematically constrained low-leakage intervention; the mechanism our forgetting arm should imitate to stay under budget.

title: Reproducibility Study of AlphaEdit: Null-Space Constrained Knowledge Editing
base_model: LLaMA-3-8B, GPT-J, GPT2-XL, Llama3.2-1B/3B, Qwen2.5-3B, Phi3-3.8B, Gemma2-2B
low_dose_frontier_quality: stable to ~3000 edits (93-99% efficacy)
near_collapse_behaviour: knee at ~5000 edits: LLaMA-3-8B BoolQ >0.8 -> <0.1 after 5000; MMLU ~0.6 -> ~0.1 by 10000; protection is bounded not unconditional
notes: Independent confirmation that even the best constrained editor has a finite knee; also tests 1-4B models (closest to gemma-3-4b) where AlphaEdit's advantage does not generalize uniformly.

title: Lifelong Knowledge Editing requires Better Regularization (ENCORE)
utility_metric: MMLU, SST2, MRPC, RTE, CoLA, NLI (every 1000 edits)
low_dose_frontier_quality: ENCORE holds downstream through 10000 edits; edit score 92.57 at 10k (Llama-2-7B)
near_collapse_behaviour: MEMIT norm grows 10x by 10k edits, edited-layer share of residual stream rises from ~1% to 7-40%, edit score ~81->~50 (Llama-3-8B); baselines degrade at 3000-5000 edits
notes: Identifies the accumulation mechanism itself: monotone norm growth = a measurable, non-un-leakable damage odometer. Norm/activation-share tracking is a cheap daily leakage meter for our runs.

title: Perturbation-Restrained Sequential Model Editing (PRUNE)
low_dose_frontier_quality: restraining condition number preserves general ability during sequential editing
near_collapse_behaviour: unrestrained condition numbers grow with edit count and progressively disrupt original associations
notes: Second independent accumulation mechanism (condition-number growth). Supports H4 lever: bounding per-day perturbation keeps cumulative damage sublinear.

title: A Comprehensive Study of Knowledge Editing for Large Language Models (KnowEdit)
low_dose_frontier_quality: current methods manage single/batch edits with minimal cognitive disruption
near_collapse_behaviour: fluency/locality degrade before edit success does in erasure settings
notes: Benchmark/taxonomy source (KnowEdit datasets incl. erasure). Useful for metric definitions (locality = our collateral); weak on long sequential sweeps.

title: CURaTE: Continual Unlearning in Real Time with Ensured Preservation of LLM Knowledge
low_dose_frontier_quality: near-perfect: TOFU stage 3 retain 0.961 vs base 0.973 across 10 RETURN stages
near_collapse_behaviour: GA retain 0.973->0.003 and GradDiff ->0.000 by TOFU stage 3; CURaTE flat because weights never move
notes: Guardrail-style baseline: zero accumulation because nothing is edited — an upper-bound control arm, but does not satisfy our weight-level erasure requirement (recoverable by removing the gate).

title: Jogging the Memory of Unlearned LLMs Through Targeted Relearning Attacks
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: 30-48 steps at lr 2e-4 suffice to relearn
near_collapse_behaviour: relearning restores near-original forget scores
hypothesis_supported: H2 threat: benign text correlated with forget topic revives erased content even when relearn set excludes answers
notes: WMDP judge score: GA-unlearned 1.27 -> 6.2 after relearning on benign articles (= original 6.2); NPO 1.0 -> 5.08; relearn success falls 100%->48%->8% as unlearning depth increases

title: Unlearning Isn't Deletion: Investigating Reversibility of Machine Unlearning in LLMs
knob_name: unlearn LR x steps; relearn data source
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: sample-efficiency hierarchy mapped (forget data > domain retain > unrelated)
near_collapse_behaviour: aggressive GA (lr 3e-5) is irreversible: forget acc 0% stays 2.1% after relearn; retain acc 1.8% unrecoverable
hypothesis_supported: supports H1 (moderate-dose damage recoverable) and H2 risk (relearning on domain-aligned retain data slowly restores forget acc)
notes: GA lr 5e-6 N=100: forget acc 9.1% -> 80% after relearn; retain recovers to 65%. Unrelated-data relearning is the most gradual recovery path

title: Invariance Makes LLM Unlearning Resilient Even to Unanticipated Downstream Fine-Tuning
low_dose_frontier_quality: unknown
near_collapse_behaviour: baseline RMU/NPO unlearning rapidly reverts under unrelated fine-tuning (e.g. GSM8K)
hypothesis_supported: H2 mitigation at forget time: training-time invariance (one anchor FT dataset) makes erasure survive later benign fine-tuning
notes: Directly models our heal-after-forget setting; ILU beats NPO/RMU on WMDP retention after downstream FT

title: Unlearning That Lasts: Utility-Preserving Robust and Almost Irreversible Forgetting in LLMs
low_dose_frontier_quality: unknown
near_collapse_behaviour: claims strong resilience to benign relearning
hypothesis_supported: if forget objective is JSD-shaped healing is less likely to revive concepts (H2 mitigation)
notes: Abstract-level claims verified; per-number extraction pending from PDF

title: Catastrophic Failure of LLM Unlearning via Quantization
low_dose_frontier_quality: n/a
near_collapse_behaviour: 4-bit quant restores 83% of forgotten knowledge on average (vs 21% retained at full precision); 8-bit benign
hypothesis_supported: H2 caveat: forgetting achieved with small utility-preserving weight changes is structurally shallow; any weight-space perturbation (incl. healing) risks revival
notes: GA_KLR on BOOKS: 13% retention full precision -> 89% after 4-bit quant; SURE mitigation uses saliency maps + large LR

title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: rank sweep 16/64/256 traces learn-forget frontier
near_collapse_behaviour: full FT perturbations are rank 10-100x typical LoRA; forgets far more
hypothesis_supported: H1 design lever: low-rank healing bounds what the repair pass can change; r=256 IFT reaches full-FT parity on HumanEval (0.498 vs 0.497) while forgetting less
notes: Supports low-rank healing pass; rank is the dose knob trading repair strength vs risk of touching erased concepts

title: Understanding Catastrophic Forgetting in Language Models via Implicit Inference
forget_metric: recovery of suppressed capability via conjugate prompts
low_dose_frontier_quality: n/a
near_collapse_behaviour: fine-tuning suppresses rather than deletes; capabilities recoverable by prompting alone
hypothesis_supported: H2 warning: both collateral damage and erasure may be task-inference shifts; healing that shifts inference back can revive the concept without any leaked data
notes: Conjugate (translated) prompts recover ICL lost to instruction tuning and harmful generation suppressed by safety FT

title: An Empirical Study of Catastrophic Forgetting in Large Language Models During Continual Fine-tuning
low_dose_frontier_quality: moderate
near_collapse_behaviour: forgetting worsens with scale (BLOOMZ 1.1b: 9.5% DK loss vs 7.1b: 18.4%)
hypothesis_supported: H1 support: mixing general instruction data during sequential FT cuts reasoning loss 31.3%->7.6% (LLaMA vs ALPACA) - healing-style rehearsal works
notes: Reading comp FG up to 27%; general-instruction-tuned start point forgets far less across sequential tasks

title: On Large Language Model Continual Unlearning
low_dose_frontier_quality: unknown
near_collapse_behaviour: baselines degrade under continuous requests; O3 stays stable
hypothesis_supported: alternative to healing: isolate each day's forgetting in an orthogonal adapter so no repair needed; retain-data-free
notes: Structural answer to sequential utility decay; inference-time gating rather than weight repair

title: FIT to Forget: Robust Continual Unlearning for Large Language Models
method_family: filtering + adaptive algorithm selection + targeted layers
knob_name: number of sequential requests; layer fraction (25%)
low_dose_frontier_quality: good: F.D./R.U. tracked at 60/120/180/300 requests
near_collapse_behaviour: GA collapses to F.D.=0.00 by 60 requests; NPO decays 0.25->0.12 by 300; overlapping gradients on shared tokens drive collapse
hypothesis_supported: H1 context: prevention (redundancy filtering, 25% layer updates) avoids cumulative damage that healing would otherwise have to repair; robust to relearning + int4 quant attacks
notes: FIT holds R.U. 0.88->0.71 over 60->300 requests on Llama-3-8B while GA/RLabel collapse by request 60

title: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting in Neural Networks (EWC)
low_dose_frontier_quality: n/a
near_collapse_behaviour: without EWC sequential tasks overwrite earlier ones
hypothesis_supported: H1 lineage: importance-weighted penalties during each day's update could protect chat-quality weights instead of repairing them afterwards
notes: Classical; Fisher information marks weights to protect - candidate regularizer for the forget pass rather than the heal pass

title: Gradient Episodic Memory for Continual Learning
low_dose_frontier_quality: n/a
near_collapse_behaviour: gradient constraint prevents loss increase on stored past-task examples
hypothesis_supported: H1 lineage: project each day's unlearning gradient to not increase loss on a stored retain buffer - a preventive analogue of healing
notes: Classical rehearsal-by-constraint; buffer must be concept-filtered in our setting

title: Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning (arXiv precursor: Maintaining Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning)
low_dose_frontier_quality: rho=1e-4 sustains plasticity to 5000 tasks; too-large rho behaves like re-init
near_collapse_behaviour: accuracy falls 89% -> 77% (linear-net level) by task 2000; ~25% dead units and rising weight magnitude + falling effective rank accompany it
notes: Canonical evidence plasticity loss is real and gradual over long lineages; gives the three cheap diagnostics (dead-unit %, mean |w|, effective rank). L2 + shrink-and-perturb was best of the standard mitigations.

title: The Dormant Neuron Phenomenon in Deep Reinforcement Learning
low_dose_frontier_quality: tau=0.1 is the reported operating point; tau=0 finds only fully dead units and pruning them costs nothing
near_collapse_behaviour: dormant fraction rises ~5-10% -> 40-60% over 200M frames; ~70% at replay ratio 2.0; dormant units rarely reactivate on their own
notes: Best-specified cheap diagnostic with an actual threshold (tau=0.1 on layer-normalised mean activation). ReDo raised effective rank 449.2 -> 470.8 and gave ~15-25% score gains at RR=1.0.

title: Efficient transformer adaptation for analog in-memory computing via low-rank adapters
method_family: noise-aware training under injected Gaussian weight noise
